name: Blue Lilac
lede: Blue Lilac is a muted violet that sits halfway between lilac and blue-violet, and Baty's color reference system pairs a similar shade with a flower, an insect and a stone.

sections.title: A lilac that leans blue
sections.body: Lilac is a pale purple named for the flower, and Blue Lilac pushes it toward the blue side [3]. The name is listed in several systems, including RAL, Ridgway and ISCC-NBS, which is why the library holds it [3]. Nearby are [[lilac]], [[violet]] and [[blue-violet]] [3].

sections.title: Baty's chart of nature
sections.body: Baty's *Nature's Palette* is a color reference system with matching examples from the natural world [4]. Under his bluish lilac purple, the examples appear to be the male broad-bodied chaser dragonfly, blue lilac blossom (*Syringa*) and the mineral lepidolite [4]. The scanned page is hard to read, so the exact pairing is a cautious reading [4].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds no painting with this violet at the usual match threshold, as photographed [2]. A color this specific is easier to find on a petal or a mineral than on a canvas [2].
